status_statement: Five of six items achieved. The aarch64 cross-build is BLOCKED by a missing host sysroot, and the container and conda recipes are written but were NOT built or linted because the Docker daemon and conda-build are absent. Nothing was published. No comparison or build in this file is claimed without having been run.

items.detail: toolchain pinned to 1.91.0, --locked verified load-bearing, two clean builds byte-identical in two modes
no aarch64 sysroot or cross C toolchain on the host; Rust target and pure-Rust crates do cross-compile, native C deps and linking do not
Docker daemon unavailable; build command and strip validated outside a container
conda-build not installed; structural checks only
deterministic CycloneDX 1.5 generated by a stdlib script from Cargo.lock; 162 components, 155 with SHA-256

toolchain.why_this_version: noodles 0.118.0 declares rust-version = 1.91.0, so 1.91 is the workspace floor; building at the floor proves the MSRV claim instead of only asserting it

locked_flag_verified.method: added an unlisted dependency to a member manifest and ran cargo build --locked
locked_flag_verified.observed: error: the lock file needs to be updated but --locked was passed to prevent this

mode_1_plain.caveat: embeds absolute source and registry paths from debug info, so it is reproducible only at the same checkout and CARGO_HOME path

mode_2_remapped.note: this is the mode a packager should use: output does not depend on the checkout location

reproducible_build.embedded_paths_evidence: strings on the plain build shows /home/rimuru/.cargo/registry/... and /home/rimuru/Projects/... ; zero after remapping
reproducible_build.functional_equivalence_checked: remapped and plain binaries produce identical --version output and identical trim output (only wall-clock timing on stderr differs)

aarch64_cross_build.blocker: no aarch64 sysroot and no aarch64 cross C toolchain on the host
diagnosis_established: the Rust target works: rustup target add succeeded and bioinfo-common, a pure-Rust member, produces a real aarch64 rlib
native C dependencies cannot be compiled: cc-rs reports 'failed to find tool aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc'
pointing cc at clang --target=aarch64 fails because clang finds x86_64 glibc headers ('__float128 is not supported on this target')
nothing can be linked: 'rust-lld: libstd-....rlib is incompatible with elf64-x86-64' and 'ld.lld: cannot open crtbeginS.o' / 'unable to find library -lgcc_s'
approaches_tried_and_rejected: cargo check with CC=clang (zstd-sys still fails at compile time)
aarch64_cross_build.conclusion: environmental blocker, not a recipe defect

container.docker_daemon_error: failed to connect to the docker API at unix:///var/run/docker.sock; check if the path is correct and if the daemon is running: connect: no such file or directory

locally_validated_steps.result: only libgcc_s, libm, libc, ld-linux; no RPATH/RUNPATH, so debian:bookworm-slim is sufficient with no extra packages

evidence_conda_build_absent.conda_render: conda: error: argument COMMAND: invalid choice: 'render'

conda.structural_check_result: PASS (structural checks only; conda-build was NOT run)
structural_checks: required sections present: package, source, build, requirements, test, about
no tab characters, no trailing whitespace, every content line a mapping entry or list item (block scalars handled)
package.version resolves to a literal, including through a {% set %}
build script uses cargo build --release --locked -p rust-cutadapt
requirements.build requests a C compiler for zstd-sys and lzma-sys

negative_control.result: FAIL: build script does not use `cargo build --release --locked`

open_decisions_documented_in_recipe: the sdist must be the whole workspace, because rust-cutadapt uses path dependencies on bioinfo-common and bioinfo-fastx, which are not published to crates.io
the conda rust package must supply 1.91.0 or the toolchain pin becomes a fiction; left as an explicit decision rather than guessed

sbom.generator_kind: stdlib Python script driven by cargo metadata --locked --offline
sbom.why_written_by_hand: no SBOM tooling installed: cargo-sbom, cargo-cyclonedx, cyclonedx-py, syft, trivy and bom are all absent, and `import cyclonedx` fails
sbom.serial_derivation: UUIDv5 over sha256(Cargo.lock) plus the sorted component list, so identical inputs give an identical serial

mechanism: no timestamp (deliberate: a clock value would make every run differ)
no hostname, no absolute paths, no random UUIDs

bugs_found_and_fixed.bug: cargo metadata does not expose checksums (checksum is None for all 162 packages), so the first version emitted 0 hashes
SPDX expressions such as 'MIT OR Apache-2.0' are not valid CycloneDX license.id values
bugs_found_and_fixed.fix: emit license.expression for expressions and license.id for single identifiers

self_test_asserts: at least 100 components carry a checksum

source_changes.change: added #[allow(clippy::unnecessary_cast)] with an explanatory comment above statvfs_free
source_changes.why: pinning 1.91.0 surfaced clippy::unnecessary_cast on `stats.f_bavail as u64`; u64::from() is also rejected (useless_conversion) on x86_64, and removing the casts would silently truncate on 32-bit targets where c_ulong is 32-bit
source_changes.verified: git diff shows only added comment lines and the attribute; casts remain

qc_differential.result: 22/22 fixtures passed; MultiQC parses without warnings

verification_attribution.note: Every command quoted was executed personally. Sub-instances in this session have no shell tool, so no independent run was possible; nothing here is a second-hand claim. One exception is noted honestly: rustup target add downloaded the aarch64 rust-std component, which required network access from rustup itself.
